nodes.title: Prove supervisor + real sessions crossing a slice boundary
nodes.evidence: Session restart cleared the permission block. Supervisor run 18:52:51Z-18:53:30Z against a throwaway 2-node DAG with the REAL session-claude.sh: spawn P1 -> rc=0 state='unit-done' -> 'self-feeding to the next node' -> spawn P2 -> rc=0 state='unit-done' -> 'DAG exhausted' -> state 'finished', sessions=2, exit 0. Boundary crossed twice with no human turn. A scratch DAG was required because the live one had no ready node, and S4b itself is self-referential (D-16).

nodes.title: Resolve project.env being unwritable under protect-paths
nodes.evidence: Narrow allowlist '(^|/)\.claude/project\.env$' checked before the deny patterns. 18/18 regression green: the two allowed forms pass, five near-miss lookalikes still deny, and all nine pre-existing protections (.env, .env.local, pem, key, ssh, secrets/, migrations, workflows, aws) are intact. Rename to project.sh rejected - it would silently break every downstream project whose hooks read project.env by name.

nodes.title: Give the supervisor mutual exclusion on a DAG node
nodes.evidence: Two fixes for one root cause. (1) supervisor.sh takes a PID lock at startup: a live holder is REFUSED before the start banner, a dead holder's lock is reclaimed, and the lock is released on exit -- all three verified. (2) session-claude.sh now runs the headless child in the background and its trap TERMs then KILLs it on EXIT/TERM/INT; previously the trap killed only the heartbeat ticker, so a SIGTERM to the wrapper orphaned a `claude` process that kept editing the repo while the supervisor believed the node was free.

nodes.title: Close the evasion gaps in block-dangerous.sh and its false positives
nodes.evidence: All four evasions closed by matching at COMMAND POSITION -- start of string or just after a separator -- instead of a bare caret, plus a git option group that tolerates both a lone flag and a flag with its own argument (the -C <dir> form was the one case that still slipped through the first attempt). The home-variable pattern now accepts quoted and braced forms. hook-checks/test_deny_gaps.py: 10 blocked / 9 allowed, where the 9 prove ordinary commands were not caught in the widening -- 'sudoku --help', a subcommand used as a word prefix, and a binary whose name merely ends in git all still pass. The suite that originally reported the gaps, test_deny_hooks.py, now reports 62 PASS / 0 FAIL. NOT fixed, deliberately: the mirror defect. Patterns still match inside quoted literals and heredoc bodies, so documenting a dangerous command is blocked as if running it -- hit twice while doing this work. Distinguishing a real invocation from a quoted mention needs shell parsing, and the shortcut of stripping heredoc bodies opens a real hole because a heredoc fed to a shell executes. For a deny control a false positive is a nuisance and a false negative is a breach, so the bias was left where it is and the reasoning written into the hook header.
